chapter_title: The Apostle is asked: Why when you drew every thing in the Picture (- Book), did you not draw the Purification of the Catechumens who shall be cleansed by Transmigration?
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by institutional discourse (catechumen vs. elect) framed as a dialogue about Mani’s Picture-Book. It lacks the impersonal, systematic cosmos→cosmos correspondential mappings that mark the oldest teaching substrate. The second half shows strong pastoral drift (explaining catechumenal purification as ‘middle way’), consistent with later community/institutional redaction. One paragraph uses distinctly Gospel/Christian eschatological vocabulary (e.g., ‘gehenna’), best treated as Christian overlay rather than core teaching.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic narrative setup (‘Once again… stood up… He says to our enlightener…’) is hagiographic/dialogue frame; no impersonal cosmological exposition.

Eschatological contrast (righteous vs sinner) is presented in Picture-Book terms, but the use of ‘gehenna’ and judicial trial language strongly suggests Christian/Gospel-derived vocabulary entering the Kephalaia via Mani’s Christian synthesis or later redaction, not the pre-compilation correspondential substrate.

Institutional focus on ‘the catechumen’ and desire for reassurance/recognition (‘know… recognised… face to face’) is community-facing and exhortational in purpose rather than cosmos→cosmos description; no systematic correspondential mapping.

Begins with explicit dialogue attribution (‘Then speaks the enlightener…’) and continues with an institutional explanation (why the catechumen’s path isn’t depicted; ends ‘with the elect’). The whole paragraph is keyed to catechumen/elect categories rather than impersonal cosmological mechanics.

Continues institutional clarification of the catechumen’s ‘middle way’ of purification (not purified ‘in a single place’). Even if it implies transmigration, it is articulated as catechumenal discipline/identity within the church scheme, not as an older systematic cosmological register.
Formulaic closing response (‘had heard… was persuaded… kept silent’) functions as narrative closure typical of the redactional frame.
